newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Barge problems small despite Rhine's part closure.
newsitem.headline: Barge problems small despite Rhine's part closure.

text.p: The closure of a section of the Rhine due to high water level is expected to cause only short-term barging difficulties, inland shipping operators said on Friday.
"For sure, there are a few problems, but (falling water) levels further upstream suggest that we will be able to sail again shortly after the weekend," one barge operator said.

Operators said a ban on sailing on the Rhine at Koblenz came into operation on Thursday afternoon and one was likely to be enforced at Cologne later today as water levels headed above the significant 8.3 metre mark.
"We can certainly sail (from Rotterdam) to Duisburg and from Karlsruhe to Basle, but most of the section in between is out of bounds," said a Rotterdam-based operator.

However, operators said barge traffic was in fact relatively thin. In cold periods, the Rhine is a key artery for the transport of heating oil into Germany, but German demand for the product has been slight as mild weather persists and prices sag.
"There were quite a few loadings (in Rotterdam) as it's the end of the month, and some barges are stuck up the Rhine, but the problems aren't too great," one operator said.
On Wednesday, German authorities suspended shipping on three major Rhine tributaries - the Neckar, Saar and Mosel.

On the same day, barges were also prevented from passing Assmannshausen, on the Rhine some 40 kilometres (25 miles) upstream of Koblenz, when a barge carrying gravel sank. Tugs had removed the sunken barge by Thursday.
